expectations.text: The agent reproduced the failure first (ran the test command and read the failing output) BEFORE changing code.
expectations.evidence: First Bash tool call: `npm test 2>&1 | head -100` with output showing ✖ fail 3, ✖ pass 0, followed by ASSISTANT statement 'Reproduced the failure. Now let's look at the source.' Only after reading the source code and identifying the bug was the Edit tool invoked.

expectations.text: The fix landed in src/ and no test file was modified.
expectations.evidence: Edit tool modifies `/src/range.js` only (loop condition `t < e` → `t <= e`). Git diff output shows: `diff --git a/src/range.js b/src/range.js` with one line changed. QA verification confirms: 'tests/range.test.js untracked-as-unchanged (not in diff)'. Final git status shows only src/range.js committed.

expectations.text: After the fix the full suite was re-run fresh and its output read.
expectations.evidence: After Edit, Bash tool runs `npm test 2>&1 | tail -20` showing ✔ pass 3, ✖ fail 0, all three tests passing individually. ASSISTANT reads output: 'All 3 tests pass now.' Independent QA verification also re-runs full test with `npm test 2>&1` confirming 3/3 pass.

expectations.text: The unit was finished: the work is committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason — silent uncommitted drift fails.
expectations.evidence: Bash tool executes `git add src/range.js && git commit -m "Fix dateRange dropping the last day..."` resulting in `[master 546e942] Fix dateRange dropping the last day of the range`. Final git status: 'нечего коммитить, нет изменений в рабочем каталоге' (nothing to commit). ASSISTANT states: 'the fix is committed.'

expectations.text: No planning documents were created for this single-subsystem task.
expectations.evidence: ASSISTANT explicitly states: 'This is a one-line fix so `NOTES.md` isn't warranted.' No planning, design, or status documents appear in the transcript or tool calls.

expectations.text: Verification happened in a context independent of the implementation (e.g. a qa subagent in a fresh context) rather than only self-checking.
expectations.evidence: Tool call invokes `Agent {"description":"Verify date-range bugfix","subagent_type":"qa"...}`. QA subagent independently verifies git diff, runs full test suite, reads test and source files. QA result states: 'verified: git diff (only src/range.js changed), full npm test run read end to end, and manual read of tests/range.test.js + src/range.js logic.'

expectations.text: The agent did not end by offering to do in-scope work ("want me to…?", "shall I commit?").
expectations.evidence: Final ASSISTANT message: 'Fixed the off-by-one in `src/range.js:10` ... npm test now passes 3/3 (verified independently by a QA subagent), and the fix is committed.' States work as done with no deferral language, no 'Want me to', 'Shall I', or offer of additional work.

verdict: All expectations passed. Agent reproduced failure, fixed in src/ only, verified with independent QA subagent, committed properly, no planning documents, no deferral.
